review: 2:3–2:4 וְהִזִּיעַ דָּמֶיךָ / כַּדָּם בַּתְּפִלָּה — Luke 22:44 (וַיְהִי זֵעָתוֹ כִּדְמֵי טִפִּים); the Arabic وَقَدْ نَضَحْتَ عَرَقًا / كَالدَّمِ فِي الصَّلَاة is that verse, and Hebrew keeps the comparison although the syntax reverses.

3:1–3:2 נִלְקַחְתָּ בְּחָזְקָה / אֶל־מִחוּץ לַחוֹמוֹת — the Arabic أُخِذْتَ عُنْوَةً ('seized by force') with Heb 13:12 (מִחוּץ לַמַּחֲנֶה); Hebrew keeps the outside-the-walls image the Arabic explains.
4:2 זֶבַח הָעֲוֺנוֹת — 'the sacrifice for sins' (Isa 53:10, אָשָׁם); the Arabic ذَبِيحَةَ الْآثَام is the guilt-offering, and זֶבַח with the plural is the closest construct at the line's length.
5:2 מַלְאָה פֶּלֶא וָפָחַד — 'full of wonder and awe'; the Arabic يُفْضِي إِلَى الْعَجَب is 'leading to wonder', and מָלֵא is used as a finite verb here for the beat.
6:4 וְאֶת־הַצְּלָב — the line is left at three words, as the Arabic الصَّلْبِ sits alone on its line after the split word; Hebrew cannot split, so the cross ends the stanza.
